correctness.rationale: For each chosen terminal active set of size k containing s seeds, m=k-s candidate nonseeds must have sorted thresholds t_(j)<=s+j-1. Circular parking functions count exactly s*k^(m-1) admissible ordered vectors for m>0, with empty case one. All other N-k nonseeds must have threshold>k, yielding P(K=k)=C(N-s,k-s)*s*k^(k-s-1)/N^(k-s)*(1-k/N)^(N-k), including k=s and k=N yielding s/N. For fixed s and k>=epsilon*N, the exact ratio to the one-seed PMF tends uniformly to s. The one-seed distribution equals binomial mass B(N,k)/k and uniform Stirling yields N^(-3/2)/(sqrt(2*pi)*x^(3/2)*sqrt(1-x)); a binomial endpoint bound controls x->1, and integrating gives s*sqrt(2/pi)*sqrt((1-epsilon)/epsilon). Dividing gives conditional density sqrt(epsilon)/(2 sqrt(1-epsilon))*x^(-3/2)*(1-x)^(-1/2), no atom at 1. Independent exact rational normalization for N<=22 and exhaustive threshold vectors N<=7 confirm finite cases only.
residual_risks: Asymptotics require fixed integer s and fixed epsilon in (0,1), not growing seeds or moving epsilon. Exact distribution assumes uniformly discrete iid thresholds on 1..N and complete mixing; this is a single movement, not network contagion.
